subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should the built-in TUI expose a persistent `ui.accessibility.plainText`-style setting, a TUI-local launch flag, or automatic terminal capability behavior, and which ASCII labels should be canonical?
rationale: The accessibility need and affected core surface are clear, but adding a durable config key and choosing replacement presentation are public product contracts rather than mechanical bug repair.

options.title: Persistent config mode
options.body: Add a documented `ui.accessibility.plainText` setting and thread one canonical symbol set through every TUI rendering path.

options.title: TUI launch flag
options.body: Add a TUI-specific CLI flag that avoids global config expansion but must be supplied by each launcher or wrapper.

options.title: Automatic detection
options.body: Infer plain presentation from terminal or environment capabilities, accepting that screen-reader needs may not be reliably detectable.

recommendation.title: Persistent config mode
recommendation.body: Add a documented `ui.accessibility.plainText` setting and thread one canonical symbol set through every TUI rendering path.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail most strongly connects this person to the original TUI and centralized tool-display contracts.
